summary: The one proposal (sell half of VTI, about $31.25 at the $360.94 mark) cuts the VOO+VTI shared-SPY-200-day-stop group from 23.5% to about 18.5% of equity and lowers the beta-based 10% stress loss from -$23.42 to about -$20.27. Two problems: the proposer's tax line is wrong, and there is a wash-sale problem. FIFO sells the two highest-cost lots for a loss of about $1.46, not $1.2. Because 0.04063 VTI shares were bought on 11-16, two days earlier, about $0.71 of that loss is disallowed and moves into that lot's basis. No lesson in learning.json names the Implicator and I have no graded calls; L9 (size VOO and VTI as one position) and L3 (check the bucket against the business) shaped how I counted the group.

checks.concentration: The sale is 0.086577 of 0.173153 shares, about $31.25. Equity is unchanged at $619.41. VTI goes from 10.09% to about 5.04%. VOO stays at 13.43%, so the 'US broad equity ETF' bucket and the shared SPY-200-day-stop group go from 23.52% to about 18.47%. One SPY close below about 729.6-729.8 (SPY is at 732.44, 0.36-0.39% above) would still trip nearly a fifth of the book. Cash goes from $71.02 (11.47%) to about $102.27 (16.5%), and the invested share goes from 88.5% to about 83.5%. Asset-class mix after the trade: single stocks 65.0% (unchanged), equity ETFs 18.5%, bond/gold ETFs 0%, crypto 0% (5% cap untouched, BTC blocked anyway). No name is near the 15% cap: VOO is largest at 13.4%, then DPZ at 11.5%. Sector buckets other than broad ETF are unchanged: Staples 16.5%, Health Care 12.8%, Consumer Discretionary (DPZ) 11.5%, Industrials 9.0% by bucket (MCO filed there; by business MSCI+MCO are one financial-data sleeve of about 8.1%), Technology 5.8%, Communication 5.3%.
checks.overlap: The trade reduces overlap. VTI is about 80-85% the same large-cap holdings as VOO, so half of it is a near-duplicate of the core sleeve. Through both ETFs, the book also already holds small slices of its own single names (WMT, IDXX, KR, VRSN, FAST, MSCI, MCO, DPZ). Trimming VTI removes a little of that double count, plus most of the book's small- and mid-cap exposure (IWM is 3.43% below its 200-day per the proposal). The trade adds to no sector or theme. If the proceeds go into Staples or Health Care after WMT's 11-19 print, as planned, those buckets start at 16.5% and 12.8%. A Staples add would stack further onto WMT/KR/SAM, which move together on down days (L3). Size that next buy against the bucket, not against the cash.
checks.tax: FIFO sells all of lot 1 (0.066052 sh at $378.34, opened 10-21) and 0.020525 sh of lot 2 (cost $375.95, opened 10-22). At the $360.94 mark that is about -$1.15 + -$0.31 = -$1.46 of short-term loss. The proposer's 'about $1.2' used the $375.22 blended cost, but FIFO takes the dearest lots first. Both lots are about 28 days old with long_term_on 2027-10-22/23, so the sale gives up no long-term treatment. Lot 3 (0.04063 sh at $368.94, 11-16) and the rest of lot 2 stay.
checks.wash_sale: risk: this is a partial loss sale two days after a buy. The 11-16 add (0.04063 sh) falls within 30 days before the sale, so it counts as replacement shares for about 0.04063 of the 0.086577 shares sold at a loss. About $0.71 of the loss is disallowed (the matched lot-1 shares at -$17.40 each) and added to lot 3's basis, to about $386.3/share. Only about $0.75 is currently deductible. Any VTI buy before about 12-18 widens the disallowance; the engine should add VTI to buy_blocked. VOO lots (10-20, 10-23, 10-26) also fall within 30 days, but VOO tracks a different index (S&P 500 vs CRSP Total Market) and is conventionally not treated as substantially identical, so I count that as a low risk, not a block. Dollar impact is small either way.
checks.summary: Approve on portfolio grounds: it lowers shared-stop weight by 5 points and stress loss by about $3.15 at no long-term tax cost. Correct the tax line to a $1.46 FIFO loss, with about $0.71 of it wash-sale-disallowed because of the 11-16 add, and block VTI rebuys to about 12-18.

stress_10pct_drop.note: VTI is -10.07 per $100, so selling $31.25 takes away $3.15 of loss. As a share of equity that is 3.78% before and 3.27% after. Caveat: the beta method credits KR (+$2.21), SAM (+$0.42) and WMT (+$0.30) with gains in a drop. Those are the negative betas L3/L4 theses call statistical artifacts, not hedges. Without that +$2.93 offset the figures would be about -$26.35 before and -$23.20 after.
